daily_brief: The day's most significant development was the dramatic mid-air attack on a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, in which a co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain and attempted to crash the aircraft before passengers intervened, forcing an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia [BBC, France 24, The Hindu]. The UAE has launched an investigation into possible terrorist links, while Israeli officials have called it an attempted jihadist attack. In a separate major story, Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike survived two lethal injection doses in a botched execution that has reignited debate over capital punishment methods [BBC, Al Jazeera, Le Monde]. Russia launched its largest assault on Ukrainian energy infrastructure since spring, killing at least five people and damaging the Trypilska power station ahead of winter [BBC]. Climate concerns dominated European news as Swiss glaciers recorded near-record ice loss of 5.5% in a single year [BBC, RFI]. Meanwhile, the Trump administration controversially obligated over $175 million in human rights funds to conservative causes abroad despite congressional objections [The Guardian], and France grappled with spreading school protests over education funding that have now reached universities [BBC, RFI].

top_stories.headline: Co-Pilot Allegedly Stabs Captain, Attempts to Crash Flydubai Flight Before Passengers Intervene
bullets: A Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv plunged 17,000 feet after the co-pilot allegedly stabbed Captain Smit Machchhar and attempted to take control of the aircraft
Passengers and off-duty pilots overpowered the attacker, regaining control and diverting the plane to Saudi Arabia for an emergency landing with approximately 150 people aboard

The UAE has launched an investigation into possible terrorist links; Israeli officials have called it an attempted jihadist attack, though PM Netanyahu said it is too early to confirm Iranian involvement
Captain Machchhar, an Indian national, is hospitalized in stable condition and has been hailed as a hero by leaders including Netanyahu and Indian PM Modi

top_stories.headline: Tennessee Execution of Christa Pike Fails After Two Lethal Injection Doses
bullets: Christa Pike, 50, survived two doses of pentobarbital during her scheduled execution at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville
Pike was taken to hospital after it was discovered she still had a heartbeat following the procedure; her lawyers said she was receiving life-saving measures
The execution proceeded after the US Supreme Court overturned a federal appeals court stay just one hour before the scheduled time
Pike was convicted in 1996 for the torture and murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer; she would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in over 200 years

top_stories.headline: Russia Launches Largest Attack on Ukraine Energy Infrastructure Since Spring
bullets: Russia struck 11 Ukrainian regions overnight, primarily targeting Kyiv and surrounding areas in the largest energy infrastructure attack since spring 2026
At least five people were killed, including a child in the Kyiv region; residential buildings, railways, and the Trypilska power station were damaged
Ukraine's largest private energy firm DTEK reported power to 8,000 homes was disrupted before being restored
Ukrainian PM Koretskyi said this marks the first mass combined attack of this scale since the end of the last heating season, as Ukraine braces for winter assaults on its power grid

top_stories.headline: Swiss Glaciers Lose 5.5% of Ice Volume in 'Catastrophic' Year
bullets: Swiss glaciers lost an estimated 5.5% of their remaining volume in 2026, the second-biggest melt on record following a hot summer and low-snowfall winter
Nearly 20% of Swiss glacier mass has disappeared in just five years, according to Glacier Monitoring Switzerland (Glamos)
Scientists warn the rapid melting threatens water supplies for farming, hydropower, and transport, while also increasing landslide risks
Glamos chief Matthias Huss described 2026 as 'catastrophic,' noting that 2% annual ice loss was previously considered extreme

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Emphasized broader implications for water supplies and infrastructure

sources.name: RFI
sources.framing_note: Featured on-site reporting with Glamos scientist describing individual glacier unlikely to survive 10-15 years

top_stories.headline: Trump Administration Obligates $175 Million Human Rights Fund for Conservative Causes Abroad
bullets: The State Department obligated over $175 million from its Human Rights and Democracy Fund to grants supporting conservative and right-wing causes globally, hours before funding expiration
Awards include a $40 million anti-communism fund, support for white Afrikaner rights groups in South Africa, and campaigns against Brazil's supreme court
The funds were obligated despite congressional holds and requests not to proceed; critics say the grants reflect Trump administration ideological priorities
Sources say awards were personally lobbied for by administration officials and reflect Vice President Vance's concerns about 'western civilizational norms'

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Critical framing emphasizing controversial nature of grants and potential interference in allies' internal politics
